lines.text: More than forty Jews swore an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul.
The plotters asked the Sanhedrin to have Paul brought down, but Paul's nephew heard and told Paul in the barracks.
The commander ordered two hundred soldiers, seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen to take Paul to Governor Agrippa.
Claudius Lysias wrote to Felix that the accusation involved questions about their own law, and he stepped in because Paul was a Roman citizen.
The soldiers brought Paul by night to Antipatris, and Felix, learning he was from Galatia, ordered him kept in Herod's Praetorium.
